news.story_lead: Punjab Police brings back wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi from Ethiopia Gurwinder aka Afridi, against whom the Punjab government had announced a reward of ₹ 5 lakh, landed at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport Punjab Police on Sunday brought wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi back to India from Ethiopia. He landed at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport early in the morning and is being escorted to Punjab by a team of the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF). A resident of Tut village in Tarn Taran district, Afridi carries a reward of ₹ 5 lakh announced by the Punjab government .
news.full_article_text: Punjab Police brings back wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi from Ethiopia Gurwinder aka Afridi, against whom the Punjab government had announced a reward of ₹ 5 lakh, landed at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport Punjab Police on Sunday brought wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi back to India from Ethiopia. He landed at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport early in the morning and is being escorted to Punjab by a team of the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF). A resident of Tut village in Tarn Taran district, Afridi carries a reward of ₹ 5 lakh announced by the Punjab government . The team escorting him is being led by AGTF SP Bikram Brar, airport sources said. Police sources described the operation as the first instance of Punjab Police securing the return of a fugitive from an African country. The operation comes amid the state police's efforts to track down gangsters who have fled overseas. To strengthen these efforts, Punjab Police has established an Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC) to coordinate with central agencies and foreign law enforcement authorities. Special DGP (AGTF) Parmod Ban and Special DGP (Counter Intelligence) are expected to address a press conference later on Sunday. Cases against Afridi Afridi's name surfaced in the investigation into the August 31, 2022, attack on a church in Thakkarpura village of Tarn Taran . Four masked men allegedly held the church's security guard hostage at gunpoint, vandalised statues of Lord Jesus and Mother Mary and set the pastor's car on fire before fleeing. In June 2024, Amritsar Rural Police arrested Jaswinder Singh alias Munshi, describing him as a key accused in the case. During preliminary interrogation, Munshi allegedly named Afridi and two others as his accomplices in the attack, Hindustan Times had reported earlier. Police subsequently began looking for the other suspects. Afridi was also named in a 2021 FIR registered at Sadar Patti police station in Tarn Taran under Sections 380 and 457 of the IPC, relating to theft and house-breaking, and Section 25 of the Arms Act. news.headline: Ex-Tech Mahindra executive shot 15 times by neighbour in Faridabad, had come home for Diwali
news.story_lead: Ex-Tech Mahindra executive shot 15 times by neighbour in Faridabad, had come home for Diwali Police say the suspect fired multiple rounds and was arrested the next day. Relatives say the families had argued over a dog and parking-related issues. A 43-year-old software company executive who lived in Singapore was allegedly shot dead by a neighbour at his Faridabad family residence late on Friday, with the assailant firing 15-19 rounds that left the victim dead at the spot.
news.full_article_text: Ex-Tech Mahindra executive shot 15 times by neighbour in Faridabad, had come home for Diwali Police say the suspect fired multiple rounds and was arrested the next day. Relatives say the families had argued over a dog and parking-related issues. A 43-year-old software company executive who lived in Singapore was allegedly shot dead by a neighbour at his Faridabad family residence late on Friday, with the assailant firing 15-19 rounds that left the victim dead at the spot. The victim was identified as Paramjith Dhankhar, 43, who was employed by Vietnam-based FPT Software Company Limited at its Singapore office and was visiting his family for Diwali . He was previously a senior executive at Indian tech firm Tech Mahindra . The suspect was identified as 42-year-old Mohan Sharma, a contractor and scrap-processing businessman. He was arrested from Ballabgarh on Saturday and his licensed handgun, with 59 live cartridges kept inside the bag used for storing the weapon, and two magazines—one of which was partially loaded—were recovered, police said. Deep Dive The two men lived on different floors of four-storey building in Faridabad’s Sector 21C. Relatives of the victim said that the two families had been embroiled in a dispute for the past three months over the Sharma’s German Shepherd pup defecating in the parking on the ground floor, following which Dhankhar’s family had filed a police complaint. “A week ago, Sharma had broken one of the three stilt entrance gates Dhankhar had constructed to avoid a dispute. He had filed a police complaint,” a relative, requesting anonymity, said. Also Read | Parking dispute turns deadly in Lucknow: 3 of a family shot dead, accused held Dhankhar is survived by his parents, wife and two children—a 14-year-old daughter and an 18-year-old son— who lived in the same building. The suspect’s family lived on the second floor, police said. On Friday morning, police had summoned Sharma to the Ankhir police post on Dhankhar’s complaint. In the complaint, Dhankhar’s family had alleged verbal abuse and damage to the entrance gate for objecting to the pup defecating in the parking lot, including over the opening of the underground water tank. “My cousin also reached there. I had got to know from my brother that Sharma had misbehaved with the police too inside the station. He issued there that he would teach him a lesson,” the relative said. Around 8.30pm, Sharma asked Dhankhar to come to the parking lot and move his car, after saying that the issue was resolved and he didn’t want any more conflict, another relative said. As soon as he went downstairs, he was shot dead, the family said. Also Read | ‘Op Safed Sagar’ veteran attacked over Gurugram parking dispute; FIR says ‘hit with iron rod ’ A senior police officer privy to the investigation, said that Dhankhar tried to save himself but Sharma opened fire at close range. “He emptied one magazine and then loaded another one and emptied it too. Overall, he had fired at least 19 rounds, with at least nine hitting Dhankhar. There were multiple bullet marks on Dhankhar’s Mahindra XUV 7XO, floor and walls of the stilt area,” the officer said. An FIR was filed, naming Sharma, his wife and two children under sections 103 (1) (murder), 109(1) (attempt to murder), 351(2) (criminal intimidation), 3(5) (common intention) and 61 (criminal conspiracy) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at Surajkund police station on Saturday. Pinta Ram, an eyewitness, who lives on the first floor, said he heard multiple loud bangs in quick succession. “Within seconds, we all heard screams and rushed downstairs to find that Sharma had shot Dhankhar dead,” he said. Ram said they rushed him to a private hospital, but doctors declared him dead on arrival. Varun Kumar Dahiya, assistant commissioner of police (crime), said Sharma was arrested from Dealer Chowk in Ballabagarh. “He will be taken on police remand. His wife and children have also been made accused for criminal conspiracy but were yet to be arrested,” Dewan said. Also Read | Man’s ear bitten off during parking brawl in Ggm, 3 booked Family members and police said that Sharma probably planned to murder Dhankhar, since he had gone downstairs with the handgun and two loaded magazines. “When we reached the spot, the handgun holster, pistol and two magazines were recovered from the stilt area by police,” Manuj Bajaj, Dhankhar’s close friend, told HT. The family said that Dhankhar had also planned to attend a nephew’s wedding in Faridabad on November 24. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Debashish Karmakar Debashish Karmakar is a principal correspondent with the Hindustan Times, Gurugram bureau. He has a vast journalistic experience of almost 14 years of covering crime, court, power, transport, administration, weather and other beats while working across various organisations. He has been covering Gurugram, Faridabad, Nuh, Palwal and other districts of southern Haryana for more than four and a half years. He has produced several breaking and exclusive stories while reporting from the ground where he maintains a strong presence on a daily basis. He writes news articles which are hard-hitting and accurate. With his strong bureaucratic sources, he frequently writes stories to expose the failure of the system forcing authorities to take necessary course-corrective steps. Besides crime, important convictions and court orders, he also writes on human-angle stories, on power issues and challenges faced by the residents on a daily basis in Gurugram and neighbouring areas. In the past, he worked for media houses like The Times of India, where he extensively reported on important government matters and daily proceedings at the Patna High Court. news.story_lead: 4 of family, including 2 children, killed in Odisha fire; short circuit suspected: Cops The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained, though a short circuit is suspected, the police said. Four members of a family, including two children aged 11 years and eight months, were burnt alive in a fire that broke out in their house in Odisha’s Jajpur district, police said on Sunday. The incident occurred around 8pm on Saturday, at Sk Nizam Uddin’s residence in Nalipur village under Badachana block of Jajpur district.
news.full_article_text: 4 of family, including 2 children, killed in Odisha fire; short circuit suspected: Cops The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained, though a short circuit is suspected, the police said. Four members of a family, including two children aged 11 years and eight months, were burnt alive in a fire that broke out in their house in Odisha’s Jajpur district, police said on Sunday. The incident occurred around 8pm on Saturday, at Sk Nizam Uddin’s residence in Nalipur village under Badachana block of Jajpur district. The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained, though a short circuit is suspected, the police said. According to local resident Ajay Kumar Samal, Nizamuddin arrived from Gopalpur on Saturday with his daughter and grandchildren. "The fire broke out when his elder daughter-in-law was cooking. His daughter, daughter-in-law and the two children died in the incident," Samal said. On being informed, fire services personnel from Chandikhol and Balichandrapur police rushed to the spot and launched firefighting and rescue operations. The deceased were identified as Nizamuddin's daughter Gul Afsa Parveen (26), daughter-in-law Tabassum Parveen (40), granddaughter Roshni Parveen (11) and an eight-month-old grandson, Jajpur Superintendent of Police (SP) Yashpratap Shrimal said. A youth sustained serious burn injuries in the incident. He was initially admitted to the Badachana Community Health Centre but later shifted to Cuttack after his condition deteriorated. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Debabrata Mohanty Debabrata Mohanty is a senior assistant editor of Hindustan Times who works as state correspondent from Odisha covering the state's politics, governance, public policy, natural disasters, environment and its society for close to three decades. With his long years of reporting from the state capital of Bhubaneswar, Mohanty has been known as one of the most experienced and credible journalists covering Odisha for the national English dailies. His reporting combines on-ground detail with deep institutional knowledge detailing the state's changing politics, governance issues, administrative reforms and the functioning of its public institutions. He has regularly reported on issues ranging from legislative developments and public policy implementation. Politics is his core areas of expertise as he closely tracks Odisha's political landscape, including the rise and transformation of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Biju Janata Dal (BJD), the two principal political parties in Odisha. His long association with the state's political establishment enables him to write on contemporary developments in a larger political context. Mohanty takes a deep interest in writing human interest stories, environmental issues and documenting the impact of cyclones, floods, heatwaves, and other climate-related events in one of the most disaster-prone states. His coverage extends to public health, governance reforms and stories on accountability of government institutions. Before joining Hindustan Times, Mohanty worked with The Indian Express, Mail Today, and The Telegraph, where he covered at least six general elections and as many assembly elections. In 2007, he was selected for the prestigious Chevening Young Indian Print Journalist Programme at the University of Lincoln, United Kingdom, where he received advanced training in print journalism. news.full_article_text:
### Ideological Debate Surrounds Vedic Rituals at DMK General Secretary's Granddaughter's Wedding

A controversy over party ideology and personal religious practices has erupted in Tamil Nadu following the wedding of Senthamarai, granddaughter of senior Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader Duraimurugan, to Deepak Ravi, son of film producer Kannan Ravi.

#### Core Objections Raised by Dravidar Kazhagam
- **Divergence from Rationalism**: Dravidar Kazhagam (DK) President K. Veeramani expressed strong disapproval regarding the engagement of priests, Vedic rituals, and Sanskrit chants during the marriage ceremony, emphasizing that such traditions contradict the founding rationalist movement's principles.
- **Contrasting Imagery**: Veeramani pointed out the inconsistency between the wedding invitation—which carried images of iconic Dravidian movement leaders—and the actual ceremony solemnized by traditional priests.
- **Call for Leadership Action**: Citing Duraimurugan's senior standing as General Secretary, Veeramani appealed to DMK Chief and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M. K. Stalin to intervene and prevent similar deviations among party leaders in the future.

#### Clarification and Regret by DMK Leadership
- **Concession to Personal Choice**: In a statement to the media on November 6, Duraimurugan expressed regret over the dispute and requested that the matter not be politicized. He explained that his granddaughter, who studied overseas and married outside her caste, specifically requested a traditional ceremony.
- **Adherence to Tradition vs. Party History**: Duraimurugan noted that while he yielded to her persistent request, his own marriage and the wedding of his son, Kathir Anand, were conducted without religious rituals and were solemnized directly by former CM and late DMK leader M. Karunanidhi.

#### Event Details and Dignitaries Present
- **Date and Place**: The wedding took place on November 1 in Chennai.
- **Prominent Attendees**: The event was attended by Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M. K. Stalin, along with prominent film personalities including actors Dhanush and Sivakarthikeyan.

### डीएमके महासचिव की पोती के विवाह में वैदिक रस्मों पर वैचारिक विवाद

वरिष्ठ द्रमुक (डीएमके) नेता दुरैमुरुगन की पोती सेंथमारई और फिल्म निर्माता कन्नन रवि के बेटे दीपक रवि के विवाह समारोह के बाद पार्टी की विचारधारा और व्यक्तिगत धार्मिक रीति-रिवाजों को लेकर एक बड़ा विवाद पैदा हो गया है।

#### द्रविड़ कड़गम द्वारा उठाई गई आपत्तियां
- **तर्कवाद से भटकाव**: द्रविड़ कड़गम के अध्यक्ष के. वीरमणि ने पुजारियों द्वारा कराए गए वैदिक अनुष्ठानों और संस्कृत मंत्रोच्चार पर कड़ी आपत्ति जताई। उन्होंने कहा कि यह द्रविड़ आंदोलन के मूल तर्कवादी सिद्धांतों का उल्लंघन है।
- **निमंत्रण और रस्मों में अंतर**: वीरमणि ने ध्यान दिलाया कि शादी के कार्ड पर द्रविड़ आंदोलन के अग्रदूतों और द्रमुक नेताओं की तस्वीरें थीं, जबकि समारोह पारंपरिक पुजारियों द्वारा संपन्न कराया गया।
- **नेतृत्व से अपील**: वीरमणि ने द्रमुक अध्यक्ष और तमिलनाडु के मुख्यमंत्री एम. के. स्टालिन से मांग की कि वे भविष्य में पार्टी नेताओं के परिवारों में ऐसी घटनाओं को रोकने के कदम उठाएं।

भारतीय एथलीट तानिया ने डकार में आयोजित यूथ ओलंपिक खेलों में बीच कुश्ती में रजत पदक हासिल करके एक ऐतिहासिक मील का पत्थर हासिल किया। इस जीत के साथ, वह यूथ ओलंपिक्स के बीच कुश्ती स्पर्धा में पदक जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय पहलवान बन गईं।

### प्रमुख आयोजन विवरण

- **एथलीट:** तानिया (भारत)
- **खेल स्पर्धा:** बीच कुश्ती (Beach Wrestling)

यह ऐतिहासिक पदक भारत में कुश्ती के दायरे के विस्तार को रेखांकित करता है, जो मैट पर पारंपरिक फ्रीस्टाइल और ग्रीको-रोमन प्रारूपों से बढ़कर रेत की सतहों तक पहुँच चुका है। तानिया की जीत भारत में युवा कॉम्बैट खेलों के विकास के लिए एक महत्वपूर्ण पड़ाव है।

news.headline: Dispute over parking, dog ended in ex-Tech Mahindra executive's murder in Faridabad; neighbour arrested
news.story_lead: Dispute over parking, dog ended in ex-Tech Mahindra executive's murder in Faridabad; neighbour arrested The victim had arrived in India from Singapore on November 5 to celebrate Diwali with his family and was also scheduled to attend his nephew's wedding. A dispute over parking space and a dog in Faridabad's Sector 21C turned fatal on Friday night when the former regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region was shot dead by his neighbour. The accused, who fled after opening fire at the victim, was arrested later.
news.full_article_text: Dispute over parking, dog ended in ex-Tech Mahindra executive's murder in Faridabad; neighbour arrested The victim had arrived in India from Singapore on November 5 to celebrate Diwali with his family and was also scheduled to attend his nephew's wedding. A dispute over parking space and a dog in Faridabad's Sector 21C turned fatal on Friday night when the former regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region was shot dead by his neighbour. The accused, who fled after opening fire at the victim, was arrested later. Paramjith Dhankhar, who had returned from Singapore just a day earlier to celebrate Diwali with his family, was shot dead by his neighbour Mohan Sharma after an argument over parking escalated. Sharma allegedly fired 15 rounds, nine of which hit Dhankhar. Parking, dog dispute between neighbours Tensions between the two families had been mounting over Sharma’s dog defecating in the parking area. This prompted repeated objections from Dhankhar’s family. The disagreement had led to several confrontations over the past few days, including an argument four to five days before the shooting. An argument broke out between Dhankhar and Sharma again on Friday night over car parking. Following this, Sharma allegedly called Dhankhar out of his house and shot him multiple times with his licensed pistol. Also read: Kochi doctor's phone reveals sexual abuse of several women after he alleges assault by Malayalam actors The two families lived in the same building, with Dhankhar’s family on the ground floor and Sharma’s on the second floor. Accused arrested from Ballabgarh Sharma had allegedly fled with his family following the fatal shooting. However, he was later arrested from Ballabgarh in Faridabad, police said. “The suspect is being quizzed and will be produced before a Faridabad court and taken on police-remand for detailed interrogation,” Faridabad ACP (crime) Varun Kumar Dahiya said. As reported by HT earlier , Dhankhar, was settled in Singapore and was working as the senior vice-president of a software company. He had arrived in India from Singapore on November 5 to celebrate Diwali with his family. He was also scheduled to attend his nephew’s wedding on November 24. Dhankar's son Shaurya Dhankhar filed an FIR under section 103(1) (murder) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Arms Act was registered at Surajkund police station on Saturday, according to police. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. news.story_lead: - Published 7 November 2026, 17:48 GMT At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. news.full_article_text: - Published 7 November 2026, 17:48 GMT At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. Three bodies were found at his home when it was searched by police. Here's everything we know so far. How did the attack unfold? The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city. Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car". Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard. - Follow live updates from Krakow A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured. People run for shelter as gunshots heard in Krakow Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the attacker, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said. The gunman was shot but is alive and has been arrested. Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment a police officer confronts the suspect on the ground before firing his weapon several times. The officer then falls to the ground, apparently having been injured himself. Moment police officer appears to shoot Krakow suspect Shop windows in the square have signs of damage, seemingly from bullets, with glass shards scattered along the floor. City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues. The suspect's car, found at the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, is being checked for possible explosive devices, police say. Residents of nearby buildings are being evacuated while the operation is under way. How many people have died and been injured? Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed, including a British national. Three victims are Polish and two have not been identified. Sixteen people, including five foreigners and the attacker, were taken to hospital. Among those being treated are two police officers who were shot while detaining the attacker. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk later said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack. One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added. Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims. What do we know about the suspect and motive? Police have identified the attacker as a 25-year-old Polish man but have not confirmed his name. The suspect was wearing "military-style attire" and had a military-grade weapon, according to a police spokesperson. However, authorities have confirmed the attacker was not a soldier. "Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle", the spokesperson added. Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home. A minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details. His home is being searched with support from counter-terrorism police. How did witnesses describe the attack? The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination. Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started. Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down. "A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises." Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend. She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice". Moment shooting heard in Krakow square What has the reaction been in Poland and internationally? Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is on his way to Krakow and is expected to give an address later on Saturday. Earlier, he said he was being kept informed by the interior minister and that police were investigating "the background and all the circumstances". Krakow Mayor Åukasz GibaÅa has signed an order declaring a period of mourning in the city which will last until Wednesday, November 11. President Karol Nawrocki said he was "deeply concerned" and was awaiting "a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these tragic events". US ambassador to Poland Tom Rose described it as a "savage and murderous attack". The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland". news.headline: Reserve Bank of India Dismisses Viral Claims Regarding New Cheque Book Rules Implementation
news.story_lead: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has clarified that viral reports claiming the introduction of new cheque book rules starting from January are fake. The central bank dismissed these unverified claims circulating on social media to prevent confusion among bank account holders. Banking customers are advised to rely strictly on official communications issued by the RBI.
news.full_article_text:
### RBI Clarification on Cheque Book Rules

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued a clarification dismissing claims circulating regarding the implementation of new cheque book rules starting in January. The central bank categorized these reports as fake, reassuring banking customers and account holders that no such changes have been mandated by the regulator.

**Key Factual Details:**
* **Official Stance:** The Reserve Bank of India confirmed that rumors regarding new cheque book regulations taking effect from January are false.
* **Public Advisory:** Customers are urged to verify banking rules and policy updates directly through official RBI press releases and verified communication channels rather than unverified social media messages.
bullet_points: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has labeled claims of new cheque book rules taking effect in January as fake.
Reports circulating regarding modified cheque book guidelines were clarified to be false.
The central regulator advised bank customers not to fall for unverified rumors on social media.
Official guidelines or regulatory updates are communicated directly through RBI's official channels.

The central bank issued a public clarification regarding viral rumors.

Mains: Impact of financial misinformation on banking sector stability and consumer confidence.
news.upsc_analysis: Prompt central bank clarifications serve to prevent misinformation from damaging public trust in basic financial instruments like cheques and ensure smooth banking operations.
